name: Epher
overview: Epher is a male figure in Scripture identified as the son of Midian and the grandson of Abraham through Keturah. His lineage places him within the extended family of Abraham, highlighting his role in the broader biblical genealogy. There is no further tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Epher means "[small] gazelle," reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew text. This meaning is directly associated with the reference in Genesis 25:4, and the name was not given by God but recorded as part of the genealogical account.
familyAndRelationships: Epher is explicitly recorded as the son of Midian, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Through Midian, he is also the grandson of Abraham by Keturah, underscoring his place in Abraham's extended family. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Epher's significance in the biblical narrative is rooted in his genealogical connection to Abraham through Keturah, marking him as part of the descendants who contributed to the fulfillment of God's promises to Abraham's lineage. Although not a central figure in the narrative, his mention preserves the record of Abraham's progeny beyond Isaac. This genealogical detail emphasizes God's faithfulness in multiplying Abraham's descendants.
